d.subject: Final handoff: Alpha3 continuity asynchronous physical-effect lifetime
d.finding: Controller transition generation is too short-lived to be the cancellation identity for asynchronous opening WakeInner. Normal opening progression can suppress a valid queued wake, while an IO-first schedule can let a stale wake escape before a same-attempt reversal is consumed.
d.shellBoundary: wakeInnerDisplay resolves the stable 1968x2184 physical inner panel and invokes hidden SurfaceControl.setDisplayPowerMode(..., 2); current source has no explicit inner-OFF compensation path.
d.recommendedContract: Use a semantic openingAttemptId/wake-intent lifetime spanning OPENING_FROM_CLOSED -> INNER_HANDOFF; revoke on true reversal/reset/release/privilege loss/destroy/new attempt/confirmed inner-active, and atomically one-shot commit immediately before the shell wake. Preserve current generation fencing for unrelated stale work.
d.next: Primary should independently reconcile against current main, then add a controlled wake-executor/facade integration test before any production integration; physical Fold7 validation remains required.
d.en: Confirmed at current Alpha3 HEAD: asynchronous inner-wake validity is keyed to controller transition generation, but that generation advances during normal opening progression. Depending on coroutine scheduling, the same opening can either lose the required physical wake or allow a wake to escape before a reversal cancels it. The handoff proposes a semantic opening-attempt wake token plus one-shot commit; no production files were changed and no physical-device occurrence is claimed.
